tools.name: rig_endpoints
tools.description: Per-endpoint GET /v1/models: which model is loaded and its served max_model_len. 'Started' is not 'serving' — this tool is what confirms an endpoint is actually answering and at what context. matchesExpected:false with models:[] means a pending adapter is not attached.

name.description: one endpoint by name; omit for all

tools.name: rig_gpus
tools.description: Per-GPU truth from nvidia-smi: memory, utilisation, temperature, power, and compute processes. 'idle' (no VRAM held, no compute procs) is what a deploy preflight should read instead of assuming a card is free.

index.description: one GPU by index; omit for all

tools.name: rig_services
tools.description: Per-unit systemd state (active/running, main PID, since when). Cross-check against rig_gpus.processes.pid and rig_endpoints.reachable: all three together mean 'truly serving'.

name.description: one service by name; omit for all

tools.name: rig_health
tools.description: Endpoint liveness per the router's health contract: GET /v1/models, timeout 3000ms, rolling consecutive-failure count. Gives the routing layer a real health signal to walk fallback chains against.

tools.name: rig_snapshot
tools.description: The single call that answers 'what is the rig actually doing right now.' Runs endpoints + GPUs + services concurrently, returns everything with one timestamp and an explicit degraded list. This is the anti-hallucination tool.
